docs.text: P1 is one 4-point portfolio sample. Its local checker provides feedback and does not create a second course mark. See the syllabus.

docs.title: AI use rules
docs.text: Use approved assistance for open work. Complete initial individual review, discovery notes and personal explanation/reflective reasoning yourself. Independent checks and oral defense are AI-off. Attach AI use once and reuse its ID.

docs.title: Estimated time
docs.text: 11 hours including both workshops, the required session dissection, verification, waiting and revision. The help checkpoint is not a penalty or an extra homework quota.

docs.title: P1: Build a minimal coding agent
Objectives
docs.text:
Explain and implement an observation-action loop (LO1): ask for an action, dispatch read, write or bash, return the observation, and stop. Predict model performance before measuring it, then use a failed check to improve your implementation.

You implement only Agent.run in agent_skeleton.py, within 300 nonblank, noncomment lines including any helpers you add to that file. The course supplies the model adapter, workspace tools, context compaction, task inputs and trace writer in lab_runtime.py. Tests do not count toward the implementation limit. You do not rebuild the launcher or its security checks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Complete Week 0 setup for the shared safety admission, launcher and approved hosted or replay access.

Keep the profile, version and digest returned by the Week 0 resolver, and the approved hosted or replay route. Run the commands below from the course checkout or unpacked student package root. Create a separate lab01-work directory in your editor and copy only agent_skeleton.py, lab_runtime.py, exercise.py and the five tasks/*.json files into it, retaining the tasks/ subdirectory. Keep results outside that input directory. Do not copy the whole private course checkout.

docs.title: Week 1: Predict, generate, verify
docs.text:
Complete the four required tasks in the calibration exercise. For each task, save your own time/pass prediction before generation; run the hosted or replay route once through its supplied launcher controller; inspect the candidate as text; and verify it with the public cases. Preserve wrong answers and technical failures. A later revision is a new attempt, not a replacement first attempt.

The required IDs are lab01-cal-001, lab01-cal-002, lab01-cal-003 and lab01-cal-005: signed sum, stable ordering, inclusive clamping, and whitespace with word order. The other sixteen catalog tasks are optional practice. Keep calibration.csv, the four task JSON records and corresponding candidates together. The linked instructions provide the exact start, finish, validation and report commands. At the first workshop checkpoint, show one prediction and its observed result. Ask for help if setup or waiting prevents you from making progress; a low pass rate is evidence to explain, not a reason to invent successes or repeat until every first attempt appears correct.

Save this set for Week 1 formative feedback. Reference the same commit/evidence ID in Week 2 and your P1 portfolio sample; keep the original attempts when revising.

docs.title: Week 2: Implement and observe the loop
docs.text:
The supplied interface is Agent(model, tools, max_steps, context_limit) and Agent.run(task) -> Trajectory. Start with one user message containing the task. For each permitted turn:

  1. Pass compact(history, context_limit) to model.chat. It retains the task, bounds long observations and drops old action/result groups when necessary.
  2. Append the returned assistant message, including its tool_calls.
  3. With no tool calls, return Trajectory(history, "final") immediately. Empty answer text still counts as final when there are no calls.
  4. Otherwise, dispatch each named tool with its arguments. Append a tool message containing role: "tool", the matching tool_call_id, and string content.
  5. If the turn budget is exhausted, return Trajectory(history, "step_limit").

Keep the full history for the returned trajectory; compact the copy sent to the model. Handle an unknown tool or refused operation with a short safe observation, without exposing paths or environment values. Do not keep calling after final.

For example, returning immediately after a write call creates the file but misses verification. Inspect completion.json: it should show the subsequent bash observation and then the final answer. Fix the stopping branch and run again into a new result directory. That revision is your first formative feedback checkpoint.

The bash tool deliberately accepts only python -B workspace-file.py with plain arguments. It runs that file through bash inside the launcher. It is not a general shell. Use the supplied verify.py commands from the task responses; imports and nested subprocesses remain subject to the same container limits.

docs.title: Verify all five tasks
docs.text:
The public tasks are course-authored deterministic replays. They isolate loop bugs from model variability; they are labelled fake/fake-v1 and are not real model measurements. Actual hosted-route calibration belongs to the Week 1 activity.

Task Work product Verification in the task create greeting.txt Exact text and final newline repair numbers.py Failing signed-sum examples now pass refactor prices.py Extracted helper preserves results cli hello.py CLI output matches its argument answer answer.txt Read two source files and check the answer

Replace VERSION and DIGEST with your resolver output. Run once per task, changing both --task create and the output name to repair, refactor, cli and answer. Every output directory must be new; for a revision use a name such as lab01-create-revised.

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST \
  --workspace lab01-work --output lab01-create \
  -- python -B exercise.py --task create

The unmodified starter raises NotImplementedError; it has no working loop yet. With your loop implemented, inspect the launcher exit code, exported product and completion.json. For each verification command, check for exit_code: 0 and stdout: "verified\n" in its tool observation. Check that the last assistant turn has no calls and stop_reason is final. An exported file alone is not proof of success. The fixed responses and public checks are visible so you can diagnose failures; copying their answers does not implement a general loop.

trajectory.jsonl is the minimal per-call trace for this replay. Inspect consecutive run.sequence values starting at zero and one run ID. Each record contains the input messages and returned assistant step; only that last step carries this call's usage and latency. not_collected fields are lengths/digests, not missing text to fill in. Use completion.json locally to understand these synthetic turns, and submit only the requested minimal trace plus your short explanation.

Also test an early final response and a sequence that reaches max_steps; explain why each stops. Use an oversized observation to check context compaction. If stuck, first check tool-result IDs, then the final branch, then the context copy. Ask for feedback before adding more tools or a more elaborate agent architecture.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
Keep one P1 work record and use the same evidence through feedback and P1:

  • Week 1 checkpoint: the four-task CSV, matching JSON records and candidates, with a brief explanation of one prediction and observed result.
  • Week 2 checkpoint: agent_skeleton.py, your tests, five minimal JSONL traces, and the required recorded-session dissection table and answers from the Week 2 activity labelled by task, work products and verification results. Explain one loop failure, its fix and the repeat check; reference the Week 1 evidence ID.
  • P1 portfolio sample: select this existing evidence, explain how the loop and tool boundary affect a result, and show one revision after feedback. Write your explanation independently; no separate comprehensive report is required.

P1 is individual. Include your own verification, even if you discussed an error with classmates. Keep one AI-use note across this practice unit and refer to its ID when reusing the evidence. Write your prediction and brief reflection yourself, without AI. Remove credentials and unrelated personal data before pushing; do not submit environment files or a full conversation export. If a required trace cannot be safely exported, record the technical failure and existing contemporaneous evidence in your same explanation, then use the course's announced supplement process.

docs.title: Grading
docs.text:
P1 is a practice unit with feedback and revision. P1 contributes 4 points to the 10-point individual practice portfolio by reusing selected P1 evidence; P1 has no separate course mark. Your independent explanation and response to feedback matter. Completing optional tasks does not increase the maximum.

The diagnostic rubric remains 100 points: task contracts 60, trajectory and limit checks 20, required calibration evidence 10, and human-reviewed readability 10. Each of the four required, internally consistent calibration records contributes 2.5 diagnostic points. Optional records cannot substitute for a required task or add points. Calibration measures consistent evidence, not how often the model was right; neither model correctness nor self-reported time calculates your P1 mark.

Use the five public checks and diagnostic feedback to revise. public_only means practice feedback; pending_human means the readability item still awaits review. Those 10 human points are within the diagnostic maximum of 100. Your instructor assesses P1 from the announced portfolio criteria and your selected work, checks, independent explanation and revision. Preserve technical-failure evidence for review; missing feedback is not a final zero.

docs.title: AI use rules
docs.text:
Yellow: approved hosted API route and course sandbox only, as linked in Prerequisites. Predictions and reflection are red: no AI. You may choose not to use AI for the loop implementation; the required model-calibration activity still needs its approved execution or an instructor-approved equivalent.

Use a truthful note in your existing explanation, for example:

P1, evidence L1-01. I used [actual model/tool] for [purpose]. I personally verified [checks and result IDs] and changed [one decision]. My reflection is my own. Week 2 refers to this same note.

If no AI helped your loop, say that explicitly and distinguish it from Week 1's model measurements. Correct mistakes in the same record rather than fabricating an earlier session.

docs.title: Estimated time
docs.text: Plan 11 hours total, including both workshops and the required session dissection: about 3 hours for calibration, 3 for the loop and five tasks, 2.5 for the recorded-session dissection, and 2.5 for verification, feedback, revision and your brief explanation. These are planning values, rounded up from the activity estimates, not measured student times or cutoffs. Waiting and help count. Seek support at the workshop checkpoints or when the plan no longer fits; reaching the time box does not automatically cost marks.

docs.title: P2: A specification review that changes the next action
At a glance
docs.text:
• Task: review one short change against its acceptance contract on your own, before any AI review; check one claim by running it, whether that shows a defect, leaves a suspicion or supports no finding; then compare your review with the supplied review claim by claim and decide what happens next.
  • Hand in: one work record with your specification finding and your code findings, or a justified no-finding for either, the check you ran with its actual output, and a comparison table. Copy the outline and replace every TODO.
  • Done when: no TODO remains; every defect you claim has a check that fails on the assigned change when run through the launcher, or is labelled a suspicion; a no-finding result lists the inputs you checked and what they showed; and every row of the comparison table cites evidence.
  • Time: three hours including the Week 6 workshop, waiting, feedback and revision.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Judge a change against what was asked rather than against what it appears to do (LO3, LO5). Separate a demonstrated defect from a suspicion, and calibrate how far a review written in the style of an AI review can be relied on by checking its claims one at a time (LO9).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Use Week 0 setup and rehearse with the Week 6 activity, which gives the supported launcher commands. Start with the local acceptance contract and assigned candidate. The student guide provides the copyable launcher commands, the supplied review and the optional live AI-review route. Copy only the public student/ files into a new workspace. The classroom fixture is rehearsal; its result does not complete P2.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Work in this order. Steps 1 to 4 are AI-off; save them before step 5 and before you open supplied-review.txt.

  1. Predict (10 minutes). Read the contract only. Write the one input you think the change is most likely to handle wrongly, or, if you expect none, the input you would check first and why. Write how long you expect the review to take.
  2. Review the contract (30 minutes). Look for one requirement that is unsupported, ambiguous or impossible to check. If you find one, quote the clause, give two readings of it, name an input that tells the readings apart, and write the question you would ask its owner. "No finding" is an acceptable answer only with the search shown: the clause you examined most closely, the two readings you tried, the input you checked that both readings treat alike, and the clauses you inspected.
  3. Review the change (45 minutes). For each finding give the location, an input, the result the contract requires with its clause, the result you observe or predict, and the consequence for a caller. "No finding" is an acceptable answer only with the inputs you checked, what each returned and the lines you inspected.
  4. Check one claim by running it (30 minutes). If you claim a defect, write the smallest check in probe.py that fails on the unchanged assigned change, run it through the launcher and keep the real failing output in probe-output.txt. If you cannot make it fail, say so and call the finding a suspicion. If you found no defect, run the check you thought most likely to fail and keep its passing output with the inputs it covers. Never construct a failure to have one to hand in.
  5. Compare with the supplied review (30 minutes). Open the supplied review now. The course team wrote it in the style of an AI review, and you are not told which of its claims hold. Fill one table row per claim, yours and the review's: who raised it, and whether the evidence confirms it, refutes it or leaves it unverified. For each supplied claim, choose the input that would show what the claim says, run it through the launcher, and record that input and what the change returned. When nothing you were given can decide a claim, mark it unverified and name the observation that would settle it. A refuted claim means the code does not have the problem that claim describes; say so, with the input that shows it. Judge each claim by its evidence, not by its author. Where your instructor has announced a live model route, one AI review is an optional extra: add its claims as further rows, and do not rerun it until it agrees with you.
  6. Decide and revise (35 minutes). Choose one: accept the change, narrow the task, obtain one missing observation, or stop. Say what evidence would change that decision. After feedback, revise one finding or the decision, and add anything both you and the review missed.

Ask for help at step 4 if the failing input or the execution boundary is unclear. The time box is a support checkpoint, not a penalty.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text: One existing work record that follows the outline below, probe.py from step 4, and its actual output in probe-output.txt. Use ai_review_comparison.en.md as that work record and review.yaml as its structured code-finding list. If you ran the optional live review, keep its short ai-review.txt response as comparison evidence. Do not add a separate report, a raw chat export or a second AI-use note.

docs.title: Grading
docs.text: P2 is one 3-point portfolio sample and supplies individual LO3, LO5 and LO9 evidence; see the syllabus. Feedback looks at four things: the specification finding is tied to a clause and a separating input, or a no-finding shows the readings tried and the input checked; each code finding is reproduced or honestly labelled a suspicion, and a no-finding result is backed by the inputs checked; each compared claim is judged by evidence, whether you end up accepting or rejecting it; and the revision responds to feedback. Agreeing or disagreeing with a review earns nothing by itself. A justified no-finding is a valid outcome where the change or the contract really has no problem; credit for findings follows what the assigned change and contract actually do, and feedback gives you a changed input if your checks missed something.

docs.title: AI use rules
docs.text: Yellow. Steps 1 to 4 and your explanation are your own work, completed before you read the supplied review or any AI or partner review. Approved assistance is allowed from step 5 onward. Attach one AI-use note and reuse its ID; if you used no AI tool, the note says so. Independent checks and the oral defense are AI-off.

docs.title: Estimated time
docs.text: Three hours including workshop, verification, waiting and revision. Record your predicted and actual time in the outline; the help checkpoint is not a penalty or an extra quota.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Task: distinguish a code defect from an unclear specification, then check the supplied review claim by claim.
  • Hand in: review.yaml, one work record in ai_review_comparison.en.md, probe.py and probe-output.txt; add ai-review.txt only if you ran the optional live review.
  • Done when: every claimed defect has real failing evidence on the unchanged candidate or is labelled suspicion; a no-finding lists the inputs you checked; the claim table cites evidence for every row, and you have chosen a next decision.
  • Time: three hours, including feedback, waiting and revision.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Review a specification (LO3), reproduce a code finding (LO5), and explain your own comparison and next action (LO9). The subject is a member activity report.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Use the Week 0 setup and execution rules. You need Python reading skills and an editor with line numbers. Static review is offline. Read the contract before the candidate.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Follow the six steps and work record outline in order. Steps 1-4 are AI-off. Save your prediction, specification finding and initial review.yaml before you open the supplied review or request AI feedback; cite that saved revision in the work record. Keep the supplied candidate and SPEC unchanged. A specification question belongs in the work record, not in the code-defect list. Quote the clause, give two readings, a separating input (or explain why no black-box input can settle it), and a question for the owner.

"No finding" is a complete answer in either half when it shows what you checked. For the contract: the clause you examined most closely, the two readings you tried, the input you checked that both readings treat alike, and the clauses you inspected. For the code: leave review.yaml as [] and fill the work record's "No code finding" section with each input you ran, what the candidate returned and the lines you inspected. "Looks fine" with none of that is unfinished work, not a no-finding.

docs.title: Run your check
docs.text:
Copy only this directory's public files with your editor/file manager into p2-work at the course root. From the course root, resolve the approved profile and substitute version for VERSION and digest for DIGEST:

uv run --project infra/hosted --locked python infra/hosted/resolve_profile.py --profile offline --json
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile offline --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace p2-work --output p2-smoke -- python verify.py
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile offline --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace p2-work --output p2-probe -- python probe.py

Use a fresh output directory for each run. The smoke helper covers only one ordinary input. Edit the literal rows, viewer, minimum and expected values in probe.py for your own claim; keep its imports, print and assertion unchanged. The fixed form lets the instructor check the same assertion against a private repair without giving your program access to teacher files. Quote the supporting SPEC clause in the work record. For a different form of probe, ask for teacher support.

Copy the launcher's actual combined stdout and exit code into probe-output.txt, including the command used. A defect needs a failing assertion on the unchanged candidate; a launcher error is not a reproduced defect. If it passes or you cannot make it fail, record that honestly as suspicion or bounded no-finding evidence. Submit the probe even then. Do not invent failing output or change the candidate to manufacture a failure.

docs.title: Compare with the supplied review
docs.text:
After saving steps 1-4, open supplied-review.txt. The course team wrote it in the style of an AI code review; it is not model output, and you are not told which of its claims hold. Each claim C1 to C4 gets one row in the work record table. For each claim:

  • a. Decide which input would show what the claim says, and what the contract requires for that input.
  • b. Copy probe.py to claim.py in p2-work, edit only its four literal values, and run it with a fresh output directory for each claim:

sh sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile offline --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace p2-work --output p2-claim-c1 -- python claim.py

  • c. Read the actual output. Write confirmed if the run shows what the claim says, refuted if the run shows the candidate meeting the contract where the claim says it fails, or unverified if none of the files you were given can decide it. Use exactly one of these three words, in lower case.
  • d. In the Evidence cell write the input as rows=...; viewer=...; minimum=... with the literal values you ran, and what the candidate returned. For an unverified claim, name the observation that would settle it and who could supply it.

This step does not ask whether to accept the whole change: accepting is decided claim by claim. When your run refutes a claim, that claim gives no reason to change the code it points at, and your row says so with the input that shows it. A refuted claim is a result, not a gap. A different problem on the same line is a different claim. claim.py is scratch work, so your step-4 probe.py and probe-output.txt stay as they are; you may leave claim.py in the hand-in, and it is not assessed. Add one row for each claim of your own from steps 2 and 3.

Record anything missed by both after feedback, choose accept / narrow / recheck / stop, and say what would change that decision. Keep discoveries you made from the supplied or a live review separate from the saved initial review. Revise the finding or decision after feedback and explain it unaided.

docs.title: Optional: one deterministic AI-review rehearsal
docs.text:
The command below is a keyless IPC rehearsal. It does not produce an AI review and cannot replace the supplied review. Where your instructor has announced a live model route, follow the approved hosted or replay command in Week 0 after saving steps 1–4:

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile offline --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace p2-work --output p2-ai --model fake -- python ai_review.py

Inspect the launcher result and exported ai-review.txt as an IPC exercise only. A hosted or replay response may supply at most one compact finding within the approved allowance; add each claim it makes as a further table row and judge it like the others. A failed or truncated response is not a completed review: retain the failure and seek support. Skipping this step costs nothing, and it never replaces the supplied review.

docs.title: Review format
docs.text:
review.yaml is a YAML list (initially []). Each entry has exactly these fields:

- file: tasks/report.py
  line_start: 1
  line_end: 1
  category: logic
  severity: medium
  comment: "Replace this format example with your own justified finding."

The example is syntax only, not a finding. Categories are logic, security, performance, maintainability; severity is low, medium, high, or critical. Use original one-based inclusive lines, one defect per entry, at most seven lines per entry. Broad ranges receive no match credit. Do not list every category at every line. Aliases, custom YAML tags, duplicate keys and extra fields are refused. Files are limited to 32 KiB each and the review to 512 entries; these are input bounds, not a target quota.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text: Submit the files listed at the top through your instructor's GitHub assignment entry. The work record contains prediction, specification finding or no-finding, comparison, revision, unaided explanation, timing and one AI-use note. No separate disclosure or raw chat export is required. Unchanged public starter files may remain; exclude caches and teacher/grader files. You are reviewing this candidate, not submitting a replacement.

docs.title: Grading
docs.text: P2 is a 3-point portfolio sample, assessed manually using the relevant rubric and the evidence described in the P2 entry. A justified no-finding or suspicion is assessed honestly; matching a review is not a grading goal. The teacher's local feedback helper reports how your findings, record structure and supplied-claim rows compare with the teacher's notes; its numbers are not course points and do not automatically determine your three points. Its location matching and structure checks cannot decide whether your explanation is correct.

docs.title: AI use rules
docs.text: Yellow: your first review, probe and prediction come before the supplied review and any AI feedback. The comparison analysis, reflection and explanation are your own. Add one note in the work record: AI-1: tool/model, purpose, saved manual-review revision, actual run evidence, or AI-1: no AI tool used; supplied review only. Reuse this note's ID instead of creating another disclosure file.

docs.title: Estimated time
docs.text: Use the six-step 10/30/45/30/30/35-minute plan in the P2 entry. Record predicted and actual elapsed time, including waiting, help and rework. Ask for help at step 4 if the input or boundary is unclear; the three-hour checkpoint is support, not a penalty.

docs.title: Change request: member activity report
docs.text:
Add report(rows, viewer, minimum=30) to export a member's activities as text. Inputs are already validated: viewer and each owner are nonempty strings; minutes and minimum are nonnegative integers; titles contain only letters and spaces. Records contain exactly owner, title and minutes. Input order breaks ties. Empty input returns only the header. Do not mutate the input.

Requirements:

  1. Include only records whose owner equals the viewer.
  2. Include durations greater than or equal to minimum.
  3. Order by minutes descending, preserving input order for ties.
  4. Each row contains title, minutes and the number of selected records with that title. Counting must take one linear pass overall; sorting may take O(n log n).
  5. Use SEPARATOR as the single formatting setting for both header and data rows. Changing that constant must change the whole report without editing the function.

The header is title,minutes,same_title with the default separator. There is no trailing newline. No filesystem, network or model access belongs in this function.

report.py is a course-authored synthetic candidate generated for this single change request. Review the supplied candidate; implementing a replacement is not the assignment. Cite its original line numbers. The supplied smoke check covers one ordinary input only; use requirements and counterexamples to assess coverage.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
• Task: audit a small evaluation of four tasks and three traces, run one approved model on it yourself, recompute the comparison against the supplied workflow-B teacher record, and state exactly what the numbers do and do not show.
  • Hand in: one work record with your task audit, trace audit, a results table that shows its denominators, and a claim with its limits. Copy the outline and replace every TODO.
  • Done when: no TODO remains, every count in your table can be recomputed from the records you cite, and every run you started appears in the table, including failures.
  • Time: four hours including the Week 9 workshop, model waiting, feedback and revision.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: Decide whether an evaluation result deserves belief before using it (LO6). Separate success, failure, timeout, repair and missing evidence; keep the denominator fixed; and say how far a small result can be generalized (LO9).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Use Week 0 setup and rehearse with the Week 9 activity, which gives the supported launcher commands. Your instructor supplies the P3 bundle in the local student/ directory: a four-task snapshot manifest with revision, split and digests; three assigned traces; and one separately verified real-model record for the same tasks. The tasks are course-original synthetic exercises. Copy only public files into a new workspace and do not fetch external benchmark instances. The classroom fixture is rehearsal; its result does not complete P3.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
1. Predict (15 minutes). Before running anything, predict pass or fail for each of the four tasks and name the trace you expect to hide a problem.
  2. Audit the tasks (45 minutes). For each task ask: can its check fail? Would a trivial or wrong solution pass? Does the prompt or a fixture reveal the expected answer? Could two careful readers disagree about what is asked? Record at least one concrete defect with the input that shows it, or a justified "none found" per task.
  3. Audit the traces (45 minutes). Classify each trace as clean, modify_tests, read_tests, or other evidence. Find every place where the claimed result and the recorded observations disagree: a skipped check, an edited test, or a success reported without a run.
  4. Run one model (60 minutes, mostly waiting). Declare the model, budget and timeout first. Run one attempt per task through the launcher. Keep every outcome. A wrong answer is an observation; do not rerun until it passes. Record unavailable cost or usage as unknown, not zero.
  5. Recompute (30 minutes). Build one table for your run and one for the supplied workflow-B teacher record: tasks declared, attempted, succeeded, failed, timed out, repaired, missing and invalid. A timeout stays in the denominator. Compare the two runs task by task, not only by total. Then recompute both pass rates over only the tasks whose checks you judged sound in step 2, and show the two rates side by side with the task IDs you left out and why. If student/records/workflow-b/ says the teacher record is pending, do this for your own run and say so.
  6. Claim and limits (45 minutes). Write one paragraph stating what these results support. Then name three things they cannot support, such as a ranking of models, a claim about unseen tasks, or a stable pass rate from one attempt. After feedback, revise one audit finding or the claim.

Ask for help at step 4 if the launcher refuses execution or the model is unavailable; do not change the executor or run generated code on the host. If no supported route exists, complete steps 1 to 3 and 5 on the supplied record, label step 4 as not executed, and keep P3 open until a route is available.

docs.title: Submission contract
docs.text:
Submit one JSON object with exactly these top-level keys:

{
  "tasks": {
    "p3-t1": "<task-label>",
    "p3-t2": "<task-label>",
    "p3-t3": "<task-label>",
    "p3-t4": "<task-label>"
  },
  "traces": {
    "p3-tr-a": ["<detector-label>", "..."],
    "p3-tr-b": ["<detector-label>", "..."],
    "p3-tr-c": ["<detector-label>", "..."]
  },
  "runs": []
}

Replace every placeholder with your own audit finding; the example does not assign any labels. tasks has exactly four IDs. Its labels are none, inflates, or deflates. traces has exactly three IDs and records detector labels: an empty list means clean; the supported single-label findings are modify_tests and read_tests. Other detector labels are retained as evidence but are not a scored class. runs is the list of raw records emitted by student/compare_workflows.py; each task appears once with attempts: 1 and a result of success, failure, timeout, repaired, missing, or invalid. Keep failed and missing records in the four-task denominator. Replace the empty runs list with the four records emitted by compare_workflows.py before submitting; the checker rejects a missing task record.

docs.title: Grading
docs.text: P3 is one 3-point portfolio sample and supplies individual LO6 and LO9 evidence; see the syllabus. The automatic checker reads the JSON contract above and returns feedback from the frozen task/trace checks; it does not assign course points. The full three-point sample is pending human review of the work, verification, explanation and revision. A low pass rate costs nothing. A high pass rate earns nothing.

docs.title: P3 student bundle
docs.text:
The required snapshot is the four folders under tasks/, identified by revision p3-ci-audit-v1 and split teaching. The public benchmark files are intentionally readable: the audit asks whether those checks can distinguish correct from incorrect code.

Run a public check from its task directory with python benchmark.py. When you show that a check is too weak or too strict, run your example against the original check; do not edit it.

Read each trace on its page in trajectories/: p3-tr-a, p3-tr-b and p3-tr-c. Each page shows the task statement, every recorded step and the final claim. The .jsonl file beside it holds the same record in the course trace format; validate one with:

uv run --locked python -m evals.trajectory.validate student/trajectories/p3-tr-a.jsonl

Use compare_workflows.py only through the reviewed course launcher. It declares the approved-hosted profile, one attempt per task, a 30-second launcher limit and a 5-second candidate-check limit, and records every result. Prepare a public-only workspace before each run:

mkdir -p p3-work
cp practice/p3/student/compare_workflows.py practice/p3/student/lab_runtime.py p3-work/
cp -R practice/p3/student/tasks p3-work/

For a full workflow-A report, run the command once per task with --task p3-t1 through --task p3-t4 and combine the four records. A workflow-B task invocation allows one repair after its check, so it never asks a single launcher run for more than two model requests. The launcher selects either the approved API or the reviewed replay route; a student without a key may choose replay and has the same score ceiling. For offline protocol rehearsal, the launcher may use --fake; each record is explicitly marked fake_provider: true and is not evidence of model quality. Each launcher report contributes one raw record to the submission's {tasks, traces, runs} contract in the P3 guide. A record is one of success, failure, timeout, repaired, missing or invalid; keep all four task records, including failures and missing evidence. Workflow B real records are teacher supplied in records/workflow-b/; do not invent them.

Resolve the published profile identity before starting. The profile and digest are public; the launcher keeps a key on the host and never passes it to the sandbox. A replay run uses the same command shape with the teacher-frozen record and its digest:

profile_json=$(uv run --project infra/hosted --locked python infra/hosted/resolve_profile.py --profile approved-hosted --json)
profile_version=$(printf '%s' "$profile_json" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["version"])')
profile_digest=$(printf '%s' "$profile_json" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["digest"])')
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version "$profile_version" --digest "$profile_digest" \
  --model replay --replay-file practice/p3/student/records/replay/p3-frozen.json --replay-digest 4bf488e4defdf87806e4212211da419d20d6ac59002b32d596d80f933ecf1886 \
  --workspace p3-work --output p3-out-t1 -- python compare_workflows.py --workflow a --task p3-t1 --route replay --out workflow-a-t1.json

The launcher writes the record on the host at p3-out-t1/workflow-a-t1.json. Repeat the command for p3-t2, p3-t3, and p3-t4, changing the host --output directory and the script --out filename. The registered P3 replay file is a fail-closed placeholder until the separately authorized teaching-team freeze is supplied; the launcher refuses it rather than treating placeholder text as model evidence. Use --model fake only for CI and protocol rehearsal; mark those records as FAKE because they are not model evidence. If the launcher refuses a configuration or replay freeze, label step 4 as not executed and record the launcher's failure category; do not claim a missing model result was a run.

A trace detector finding is a signal for you to review, not a verdict. Judge every flagged step against that trace's task statement and recorded results.

docs.title: Workflow B teacher records
docs.text:
Teacher records are pending. The development path uses the same protocol with a FAKE broker so the report shape, failure categories and comparison table can be rehearsed without a key:

mkdir -p p3-work
cp practice/p3/student/compare_workflows.py practice/p3/student/lab_runtime.py p3-work/
cp -R practice/p3/student/tasks p3-work/
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST \
  --model fake --workspace p3-work --output workflow-b-fake \
  -- python compare_workflows.py --workflow b --route fake --fake --out workflow-b-fake.json

The launcher writes the record on the host at workflow-b-fake/workflow-b-fake.json.

This file is development evidence only. It is marked fake_provider: true, is not a teacher record, and must not be used to claim a model result or completed student evidence.

If the launcher refuses a task (including a missing broker or an unavailable replay freeze), label step 4 as not executed and write the refusal category in the work record; do not retry by running the generated code on the host. The protocol is one attempt, a 30-second launcher limit, a 5-second candidate-check limit, and at most two model requests for one workflow-B task (the repair is the second request).

The teaching team will supply workflow B's records: a real run on an approved device, with the same model, profile digest, task snapshot and time limit as workflow A, and the repair call counted in usage and cost. The team checks the run's patches and public-test outcomes, then freezes the protocol and original records, with their reviewed digests, under practice/p3/student/records/replay/p3-frozen.json. A FAKE or synthetic record never fills this slot.

When supplied, view the summary before predicting which workflow is better. Until then, record "teacher records pending"; do not invent a comparison or a winner.
