docs.title: Project scoring and appeals
docs.text:
The project is individual: there is no contribution adjustment, and your project score is your own 0–20.

Your ci-dashboard project is scored individually across five milestones: M0 2, M1 6, M2 6, M3 3 and M4 3, for 20 points. The public project rubric defines the evidence, whole- or half-point partial credit and zero-credit boundaries. Your open-source contributions, C1 and C2, are scored with the contributions rubric and use the same review and appeals process.

The teaching team records the score from your submitted revision and evidence IDs. A second calibrated reviewer checks the evidence mapping, arithmetic and boundary decisions. Keep an unresolved or contradictory item pending while it is reviewed; missing future work is not silently turned into zero.

Appeals follow the assessment and appeals process. Submit the revision, evidence IDs, a short explanation of the disputed criterion and the specific check that supports your request. Do not include keys, raw participant material or private code.

The project score is not inferred from code volume, commit count, model-finding count, rankings, awards or oral-defense evidence. M3 measures runnable verification evidence, support for each conclusion, clear uncertainty boundaries and one self-check; the number or severity of model findings does not determine that score.

docs.title: Help with setup and learning
docs.text: Use the available-materials navigation for the Week 0 setup and fallback guides. They distinguish an offline tooling check from the runtime check that shows you can run the practices. If a safety check fails, stop agent execution and report its safe failure category. Do not work around it with host execution, network access, a Docker socket mount or elevated privileges.

docs.title: Prepare a useful help request
docs.text:
Record the course version, operating system, command mode, safe error category, what you expected, what happened, and the smallest verification you tried. Share a minimal synthetic example when possible. Inspect any excerpt before sharing it: exclude credentials, environment dumps, personal data, unrelated conversations and teacher assets. Keep setup, waiting and help time in your existing work record so the course can address the actual workload.

The Week 0 published estimate is three hours including setup, primer, diagnosis and safety checks. Reaching it is a prompt to seek support, not a grade penalty or permission to skip the launcher. Do not buy equipment, API credit or a personal key to compensate for unavailable course access.

docs.title: Teaching contact and access
docs.text:
This repository does not configure a teaching contact, office-hour schedule, student equipment application route or accommodation request channel. Those services are unavailable until the adopting course publishes real contacts, capacity and arrangements. No sample address constitutes an application route.

Once your course supplies its real support channel, use it for installation failures, device or accessibility needs, clarification, and assessment questions. The course must provide an equivalent supported path; approved alternatives retain the same learning outcomes and attainable grade. Formal assessment, regrade and appeal services require their actual published policy and entry. Missing or future assessments are not zero marks, and public practice feedback is not a formal grade.

docs.title: While access is unavailable
docs.text: Read the available conceptual material and reason about its synthetic examples. If the verified launcher is available, its FAKE broker can support protocol practice; label that evidence as FAKE. It cannot substitute for a required real-model run or for the Week 0 runtime check. If the launcher is unavailable, keep generated code unexecuted and retain the failure description for the actual course support team.

docs.title: Course syllabus
docs.text: Read the course syllabus.

docs.title: Assessment and appeals
docs.text:
Read the current syllabus for weights, passing conditions and equivalent resits. Each work record contains the artifact, verification, your own explanation and one AI-use note. Reuse evidence between a practice unit and its project milestone.

The two AI-off checks and individual defense establish independent ability. Project quality cannot substitute for the independent passing requirement. A future or missing assessment is not a zero and cannot establish a completed course result.

Receive feedback before the next related acceptance. If you disagree with a judgment, identify the criterion and evidence you want reconsidered and use the teaching team's published appeal route. Suspected inconsistency requires human examination and an opportunity to respond. No writing-style detector decides authorship or guilt.

The adopting teaching team supplies actual submission dates, reassessment appointments, approved accommodations and appeal contacts before teaching. Ask the team for these arrangements if they are not yet provided.

docs.title: CP1: individual diagnosis, test and repair
docs.text:
CP1 is a 30-minute, 10-point, individual, closed-book, AI-off paper in Week 5. It asks you to locate a reported defect in an unfamiliar ci-dashboard path, write a contract-based regression test, describe a minimal repair and protect other callers. The marking categories may be public so that the task is accessible and predictable.

The actual code excerpt, planted change, distinguishing input, line numbers, trigger observations and answer remain private teacher material. Public practice teaches the defect category and the verification method; it does not reuse a CP1 instance. The question shape may be public; the instance is not.

If the initial CP1 result is below 50%, one equivalent resit is available after feedback. It keeps the same learning outcomes, time and difficulty. The replacement is capped at 5/10, and the effective mark is the higher of the original and capped replacement. An approved invalid sitting is replaced without using the resit opportunity; a valid pass cannot be retaken for a higher mark. Both records remain. CP1 results do not change model access.

docs.title: CP2: individual unfamiliar-code review
docs.text:
CP2 is the Week 11 individual checkpoint. It lasts 30 minutes and is completed on paper, without AI, agents, devices or reference material. You review an unfamiliar code listing, identify evidence-backed defects, and give a bounded recovery and verification argument. The paper and answer sheet are collected at the end; project work cannot substitute for this individual evidence.

After feedback, an initial CP2 mark below 5/10 permits one equivalent resit with the same construct, timing and difficulty. The replacement mark is capped at 5/10 and the original attempt remains recorded; the effective mark is the higher of the original mark and the capped replacement mark. A technical failure or an approved accommodation failure is replaced by an equivalent sitting and does not consume the resit. Ask the teaching team for the published appointment and accessibility arrangements.

Request a review by naming the rubric point and the evidence on your script. A person reviews the evidence and gives you an opportunity to respond; no writing-style or authorship detector decides the mark. The teaching team publishes the review contact and response timetable before teaching.

docs.title: Fallback checklist
docs.text: Use this checklist when the API route is closed, you have no key, you chose replay, or the launcher checks fail. The route and key rules are in Week 0 setup. Work through the section that matches your launcher check result; each item says what to keep.

docs.title: When the launcher checks pass
docs.text:
These items need "can_run_practices": true from the launcher checks and no model.

  1. Smoke test and diagnostic. Run the verify.py smoke test and both diagnostic commands. Keep the smoke JSON, your answers.json and the diagnostic feedback.
  2. Primer with the supplied candidate. Do the primer exercise with the course's faulty candidate.py: keep the failed baseline, repair the candidate yourself, run the checks again and label the candidate supplied.
  3. Week 1 model steps. Where Week 1 asks for a model candidate, use the Text participation exercise in the Week 1 workshop. Record each model task you could not run as not executed; never enter hand-worked values as measured results. Run those tasks when a model route opens.

docs.title: When the launcher checks fail
docs.text:
1. Paper reasoning. For each assertion in the primer's check_generated.py, write the value the supplied candidate returns and whether the assertion passes. Record the primer as not executed.
  2. Failure category. Keep failed_probe, failed_invariant and failed_exception from doctor.py --runtime, apply the fix listed in If a check fails, and bring anything else to course support. Once doctor.py --runtime passes, continue from the first list.

docs.title: From a plausible answer to checked work
docs.text: This course-authored primer takes thirty minutes. It makes no benchmark, price or industry performance claims. Read Week 0 setup first; it contains the one account, key, budget and replay explanation used by the course.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
Explain the difference between a language model and an agent (LO1). Identify evidence that supports a generated answer (LO5). Describe why tools need a workspace boundary and a stop condition (LO2, LO7).

A language model produces a response from the context it receives. Fluent text can still be wrong. An agent adds a program around the model: observe, request, validate, call an allowed tool, inspect its result and decide whether to continue. The program owns permissions and stop conditions; a model request is never permission to read every file on your computer.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
Consider: “Given two integers, return the larger value; equal values are returned unchanged.” Before asking for a candidate, write the prompt and predict the outputs yourself. Save the prompt as prompt.txt:

Write only a Python function larger_of_two(a, b). Inputs are integers (not booleans).
Return the greater input, or that same value when equal. Negative integers are valid.
No input(), printing, imports, Markdown or explanation.

When a model route is open, this small generator sends the prompt and keeps the response as evidence. Save it as generate.py:

from pathlib import Path
from sandbox_model import chat, emit_artifact

response = chat(Path("prompt.txt").read_text())
Path("response.txt").write_text(response)
emit_artifact("response.txt")
print("Saved model response; verification is still required")

The course supplies a deliberately faulty candidate that always returns the first input. Save it as candidate.py:

def larger_of_two(a, b):
    return a

Before running anything, choose an input where the candidate and the requirement disagree. The checks below cover larger-second, larger-first, equal and negative inputs. Their expected values come from the requirement, not from generated text. Save them as check_generated.py:

from candidate import larger_of_two

assert larger_of_two(3, 7) == 7, "second input is larger"
assert larger_of_two(9, 4) == 9, "first input is larger"
assert larger_of_two(5, 5) == 5, "equal inputs"
assert larger_of_two(-8, -2) == -2, "negative inputs"
print("PASS: four specified cases")

docs.title: Hands-on exercise
docs.text:
1. Prepare. Follow setup until doctor.py --runtime reports "can_run_practices": true. Create a week0-guided directory that contains only the four files above.

2. Run the checks against the supplied candidate.

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace week0-guided -- python check_generated.py

Expected result: the run fails. The launcher JSON shows "exit_code": 1, and its stdout includes AssertionError: second input is larger. Save that JSON as your failed baseline.

3. Add your own check. Above the print line, add one assertion with an input you chose and the value the requirement gives for it. Then run the checks and keep both files through the launcher:

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace week0-guided --output week0-verified-01 -- python -c 'import check_generated; from sandbox_model import emit_artifact; emit_artifact("candidate.py"); emit_artifact("check_generated.py")'

Expected result: it still fails with AssertionError: second input is larger and "exit_code": 1, because the candidate has not changed. The launcher creates no week0-verified-01 directory, since it saves files only from a passing run.

4. Replace the candidate. If hosted.status is available and you chose the API route, ask for one candidate:

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --model api --hosted-config HOSTED_CONFIG --key-file ~/.config/course/hosted-key --workspace week0-guided --output generation-01 -- python generate.py

The API route returns text only. Read generation-01/response.txt, copy the proposed function into candidate.py and label the evidence api. Otherwise, including when you chose replay, repair the supplied candidate.py yourself and label it supplied; this primer has no replay record.

5. Check again. Run the command from step 3 with --output week0-verified-02. Expected result for a correct candidate: "exit_code": 0, stdout includes PASS: four specified cases, and week0-verified-02 holds candidate.py and check_generated.py. If your own check fails, decide whether the candidate or your expected value is wrong. If a model candidate fails a check, keep that failure: it is a finding, not a mistake in your work.

If the launcher is unavailable, follow the fallback checklist.

docs.title: Verify and explain
docs.text: Keep the candidate, failed baseline, passing or failing checks and a brief explanation under one evidence ID. State which input exposed the defect and what check you added. Include the single AI-use note required by course policy. Do not submit a key, full conversation or host environment dump.

docs.title: Set up, generate, then verify
docs.text:
Week 0 prepares you to explain a model response, test a small program and keep an agent inside its workspace (LO1, LO2 and LO7). Budget three hours for setup, the primer, the diagnostic and safety checks together. If access or waiting consumes that time, use the fallback checklist.

This page is the single student entry point for the sandbox checks, the approved hosted API route, key handling, per-run request and token limits and the replay alternative. Other student pages link here instead of repeating those rules.

docs.title: Prepare trusted course tools
docs.text:
Use a reviewed checkout or audited student ZIP. Install Python 3.12, uv, Git and a local Docker engine that runs Linux containers, through your institution's supported path. The course runs these checks on a Linux x86-64 computer with a local Docker engine. On any other computer, run the same checks; if one fails, keep what it reports and use the fallback checklist.

All generated code, shell commands and dependency scripts run through the course launcher; do not run an unknown repository command on the host. Run these course tools from the course root, in this order:

python3 --version
uv --version
git --version
docker info --format '{{.OSType}}/{{.Architecture}}'
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked python scripts/doctor.py
uv run --locked python scripts/prepare_sandbox.py
uv run --locked python scripts/doctor.py --runtime

docker info prints linux/ and your computer's architecture, for example linux/x86_64. If it prints an error instead, start the Docker engine before you go on.

prepare_sandbox.py is the one step that needs network access. It downloads only the pinned sandbox image for your engine's platform and runs no student code; a first download can take several minutes. On success it prints one line, here for a Linux x86-64 engine:

Pinned sandbox image for linux/amd64 is available; run the runtime checks next.

If it prints Sandbox preparation failed: instead, the rest of that line names the cause. Fix that cause and run it again. Sandbox runs afterwards use that image with no network and never download anything.

docs.title: Check that you can run the practices
docs.text:
doctor.py on its own checks your tools and the course configuration; it starts no container. doctor.py --runtime also runs the launcher's safety checks: workspace boundaries, blocked network access, resource limits, log redaction and prompt-only IPC.

You can run the practices when doctor.py --runtime prints "status": "passed" and "can_run_practices": true. That covers every launcher exercise: the smoke test and diagnostic below, the primer with its supplied candidate, and lecture fixtures that use FAKE, the course's scripted model replies. It does not depend on a key. A step that asks a model for a new candidate also needs an open model route: the API route with your own key, or a published replay record. The hosted and replay fields of the same output say which route is open; "status": "disabled" under hosted means the API route is closed.

Every launcher run repeats these safety checks before your command starts. One check waits out the 30-second run limit, so each launcher run takes at least half a minute.

docs.title: If a check fails
docs.text:
If doctor.py reports false for a tool under checks, install that tool and run it again. doctor.py --runtime reports a launcher failure as failed_probe, failed_invariant and failed_exception; it never prints raw Docker or workload output. A launcher run whose safety checks fail shows the same value as invariant= inside its details field. Look up failed_invariant:

failed_invariant Cause What to do boundary_probe_completion with failed_exception FileNotFoundError The docker command is not installed or not on your PATH. Install a local Docker engine, check that docker info works in the same terminal, then rerun. docker_context The docker command could not read its current context. Run docker context ls, select a local context with docker context use NAME, then rerun. local_docker_engine Docker points at a remote engine; the sandbox accepts only a local one. Select a context whose endpoint starts with unix://, then rerun. pinned_image_available The pinned sandbox image is missing, or the engine is not running. Start the engine, run prepare_sandbox.py again, then rerun. docker_engine_available The engine stopped answering. Restart the engine, wait until docker info works, then rerun. native_engine_platform The engine does not run Linux containers, or its architecture is not one the sandbox accepts. Use a local engine that runs Linux containers natively; the sandbox never uses emulation. Without one, use the fallback checklist. pinned_image_platform The prepared image is for another platform, for example after you switched engines. Run prepare_sandbox.py again, then rerun. container_start Docker refused to start the sandbox container. Restart the engine and check its disk space and memory, then rerun. any other value A safety boundary did not hold. Stop. Bring failed_probe, failed_invariant and failed_exception to course support.

Never enable network access, add privileges, mount the Docker socket or enlarge limits to make a check pass.

docs.title: Select the approved configuration
docs.text:
The course resolver is the sole source of profile identity, endpoint, model, sampling, and request/token limits. Save its output once and print the two values that launcher commands need:

uv run --locked python scripts/hosted_profile.py --profile approved-hosted --json > week0-profile.json
uv run --locked python -c 'import json; p = json.load(open("week0-profile.json")); print("VERSION", p["contract"]["version"]); print("DIGEST", p["models_sha256"])'

In every launcher command, replace VERSION and DIGEST with the two printed values. Never override an endpoint, model, header, sampling parameter or limit. Until the hosted payload is enabled, the resolver output is marked enabled: false; keep the public version/digest and follow the fallback checklist. When the hosted payload is enabled, the reviewed setup flow supplies HOSTED_CONFIG from that resolver output. Do not create, edit or substitute this file; a student-controlled configuration is rejected by the launcher.

docs.title: API route and key handling
docs.text:
If you choose the API route, register with one approved configuration listed by the resolver and create a key in your own provider account. Store it on your own device in a file outside Git and outside every course workspace. Create an empty private file first:

mkdir -p -m 700 ~/.config/course
install -m 600 /dev/null ~/.config/course/hosted-key

Open ~/.config/course/hosted-key in your editor, paste the key as the only line, and save. Then check the file without printing the key:

uv run --locked python scripts/doctor.py --key-file ~/.config/course/hosted-key

Under hosted, "key": "available" means the file is usable. invalid means the file is empty, holds anything besides the key on one line, sits inside the course folder, or other users can read it or its folder. If your editor changed its permissions, run chmod 600 ~/.config/course/hosted-key.

The launcher host-side broker reads that file. The key never enters the sandbox environment, filesystem, prompt, trajectory, screenshot, output or log. Do not put it in an argument or ordinary environment variable. A shared Docker host is replay-only; do not store a personal key there. If a key is ever committed or pasted into a prompt, screenshot or log, revoke it with the provider immediately and notify the teaching team.

Each real run uses the resolver's published request and token limits; the launcher enforces those per-run limits. Ask your provider about its own spending limit or prepaid credit before using a personal key. The broker records provider usage for the run and never prints the key. A missing, invalid or unreachable key route has a fixed failure category; then use the replay route or the fallback checklist.

docs.title: Replay route
docs.text:
You may choose replay without giving a reason. When a reviewed teaching record is available, the student launcher replays the same task through course_llm. Write predictions first, inspect the replay, recompute the checks and explain the result in your own work. Mark replay evidence in P1. Its score ceiling is identical to the API route and it is not a real API call.

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --model replay --replay-file REPLAY_FILE --replay-digest REPLAY_DIGEST --workspace week0-work -- python generate.py

This is a template. After the teaching team publishes a frozen record, replace REPLAY_FILE and REPLAY_DIGEST with the supplied path and digest. Until then, do not run it: the public file is a synthetic placeholder, and the launcher refuses it before starting a container. Keep the JSON result and verification together; inspect any model suggestion and run proposed code through the launcher again.

docs.title: Run a small isolated exercise
docs.text:
Create a separate week0-work directory containing only public exercise files. Symlinks, special files, host paths, credentials and teacher assets are refused. Dependencies cannot be downloaded inside the sandbox. Save this smoke test as verify.py:

from pathlib import Path
from sandbox_model import emit_artifact

Path("result.txt").write_text("verified\n")
assert Path("result.txt").read_text() == "verified\n"
emit_artifact("result.txt")

Run the verification through the launcher:

sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace week0-work --output week0-smoke -- python verify.py

Expected result: the launcher prints JSON with "exit_code": 0, and week0-smoke/result.txt contains verified. The launcher saves files only from a run that exits with 0, and only into a new --output directory.

docs.title: Diagnostic and primer
docs.text:
Copy the public diagnostic files into a new workspace and run them through the same launcher:

mkdir week0-diagnostic
cp assessment/diagnostic/run.py assessment/diagnostic/questions.json week0-diagnostic/
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace week0-diagnostic -- python run.py
sh scripts/course-sandbox --profile approved-hosted --version VERSION --digest DIGEST --workspace week0-diagnostic -- python run.py --answers answers.json

The first command prints the questions. Before the second, create answers.json in week0-diagnostic with your editor. This is public formative feedback, not a threshold or an official grade. Follow the primer before asking for model output.

docs.title: Troubleshoot and submit
docs.text: If the resolver or a launcher run fails, keep the fixed category and use If a check fails. If the API route is unavailable, use replay or the fallback checklist. Keep the work product, verification and a brief explanation together with one AI-use note; do not submit keys, full conversations or environment dumps.

docs.title: course_llm: generate once, then verify
docs.text:
course_llm is the shared offline interface used by the course launcher. It returns text and tool-call requests; it never executes generated code or tools. Student programs send only a prompt through the launcher’s prompt-only IPC. The host-side broker applies the approved course configuration and keeps any credential on the host; the sandbox receives neither credentials nor provider connection details. Generated code and shell commands must be checked and run through the launcher.

Follow Week 0 setup for admission, launcher use and the approved access or replay route. This page deliberately documents the package contract, not host configuration.

docs.title: Start offline
docs.text:
The default scripted provider needs no network or credential:

uv run course-llm ping --provider fake --trace /tmp/course-ping.jsonl
uv run course-llm cost /tmp/course-ping.jsonl
uv run pytest src/course_llm -q

A successful ping prints OK without printing a response, configuration or request body. cost validates each trajectory line and prints USD <amount>. These commands create only synthetic evidence; remove temporary traces after checking them.

from course_llm import Client, FakeProvider, TracePolicy, Tracer
from course_llm.trajectory import validate_record
import json
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("/tmp/course-example.jsonl")
with Client(
    FakeProvider([{"content": "synthetic answer"}]), tracer=Tracer(path, TracePolicy())
) as client:
    response = client.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "synthetic question"}])
    assert response.content == "synthetic answer"  # Verify the generated result.
for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
    validate_record(json.loads(line))  # Verify the recorded evidence separately.

docs.title: Replay and the launcher boundary
docs.text:
Replay is an equal learning route when a hosted run is unavailable. Use the reviewed record and the launcher command supplied by Week 0; choose replay without explaining why. Write a prediction first, inspect the returned text, run the local checks, and record that the result came from replay. A replay is not a new model call.

A typical replay invocation has this shape; copy the concrete version, digest and reviewed record path from the setup page or the teaching team:

sh scripts/course-sandbox \
  --profile approved-hosted \
  --version VERSION \
  --digest DIGEST \
  --model replay \
  --replay-file REPLAY_FILE \
  --replay-digest REPLAY_DIGEST \
  --workspace example-work \
  -- python generate.py

The broker accepts a bounded prompt and returns text only. It rejects extra fields, direct URLs, credentials, tools, shell commands and requests that exceed the per-run limits. The sandbox cannot read the host broker’s configuration. Inspect the proposed result and run the verifier as a separate step; a generated answer never counts as its own verification.

docs.title: Public interface and tool calls
docs.text:
Client.chat(messages, tools=None, **opts) -> Response is synchronous and non-streaming. Response contains content, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens, tool_calls and decimal cost_usd. Response.message() returns the assistant message needed for the next request. Close the client with with Client(...) or close().

Messages use {"role": "user", "content": "..."}. Supported roles are system, user, assistant and tool; every message must have string content. An assistant message containing only tool calls still has an explicit empty string. A tool definition is {"name": "read", "description": "...", "parameters": {"type": "object", ...}}. A tool request is {"id": "call-1", "name": "read", "arguments": {"path": "fixture.txt"}}. After a request, the caller validates the name, arguments and workspace permission before the launcher executes anything. Package tests use fixed tool results and perform no shell or file operations.

The scripted fake provider accepts a JSON/YAML script, a Python list or a callable. Script items can assert exact messages and tools before returning a fixed response. An exhausted script or failed assertion raises an error without echoing the hidden content. Fixed scripts make local checks reproducible and require no network.

docs.title: Budget and evidence
docs.text:
The launcher bounds prompt size, request count, output size and wall-clock time for each run. Budget also prevents a client from reserving more output than the run allows. A rejected reservation sends no request. A completed call records usage and status; an uncertain call is recorded as uncertain and is not silently retried. These are conservative local checks, not a promise about a remote bill.

Use the supplied FakeProvider or a reviewed replay in tests and ordinary offline work. Do not add another model route, call a provider directly, or put connection details in a student script. Any real route is selected by the host-side broker and documented in the central setup page.

docs.title: Minimal traces and filtering
docs.text:
TracePolicy() defaults to minimal. Each message, argument and tool result keeps only its state, encoded length and digest. An explicit redacted policy may retain fixed synthetic content; every string outside its allowlist is replaced in full, as are sensitive scalar values. Never build an allowlist dynamically from a user message or a model response.

The tracer always filters credential patterns, personal identifiers, long identifiers, course canaries and other registered sensitive values. Raw requests, responses and tool results are application data, not safe logs. Minimal trajectories cannot reconstruct a conversation, and a digest cannot recover the original value.

docs.title: JSONL contract
docs.text:
The canonical schema is evals/trajectory.schema.json. The package includes a byte-identical copy for offline validation. Each line represents one call, not a cumulative snapshot:

  • schema_version is "1"; run records a random id, sequence, model label, status, timestamp, trace policy and cost status.
  • steps records the input snapshot and returned assistant message. Only the returned step has this call’s usage and latency; other steps use null, which is not zero usage.
  • A missing value is distinct from a redacted value. Consumers must preserve that distinction.
  • Unknown cost is recorded as unknown and cannot be reported as a completed total.

validate_record checks the schema and state rules. It does not prove that a log is authentic or that a human has reviewed it. Keep only the minimum synthetic evidence needed to explain the work and run the local verifier again after any change.

docs.title: Safe log handling
docs.text: Keep traces in a controlled course workspace, restrict access, and delete temporary files and known copies after verification. Do not submit environment files, credentials, raw interviews, or full tool output. If private content appears, stop, remove the copy and use the course reporting route. Passing schema validation does not replace a privacy check or an explanation of what was verified.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Record the decision ID, responsible role and related task.

docs.title: Records
docs.text: Context and constraints; candidate approaches; choice and rationale; how assumptions were verified after generating an approach; rollback conditions; evidence paths.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: Review roles, comments, version digest and unresolved items; awaiting human completion.

docs.title: Teaching feedback scaffolding
docs.text:
• Observable behavior: (Describe an action the learner can demonstrate, its LO and verification evidence.)
  • Failed version of the same task: (Retain the input, generated result and evidence of failed verification.)
  • Diagnosis: (Use evidence to locate an assumption or implementation problem, rather than only copying an error message.)
  • Improved version: (Record revision differences; re-verify the same input and boundary inputs.)
  • Timebox and checkpoints: (Expected minutes; inspect artifacts at the checkpoint; when stuck, record the current state and ask for help.)
  • Hint ladder: (Begin with a question that locates the problem, then a related concept, then partial steps; record the level actually used.)
  • Formative feedback: (At least once; feedback source, time, evidence and actionable advice, to be completed.)
  • Visible revision: (At least once; before/after differences and re-verification results, to be completed; reuse the current file or existing activities.)
  • Teaching/rehearsal evidence: (Awaiting human completion; record pseudonymous roles, environment, timing, accessibility issues, failures and references to repair evidence.)

These fields serve teaching feedback only. They do not add weekly required files or change the eight-dimension rubric or grading contract. The template's existence, complete fields or passing automated checks do not mean that human teaching/rehearsal, calibration or approval has taken place.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text:
Complete this once in the existing description for each assignment or milestone. PRs reference the same evidence ID. There is no separate submission of this file or repeated signature requirement.

  • Assignment or milestone and evidence ID:
  • AI use: none; or the tool/model, purpose and verification I personally completed.
  • Artifact, verification results and brief explanation: reference existing paths without copying the content.

Only when this practice unit explicitly requires trajectories, include the required redacted excerpts or their paths; do not export the entire chat. Remove keys, unrelated personal information and unauthorized data. If required evidence encounters a technical failure, describe the impact and available alternative evidence in the same note and follow the course's supplementary-evidence process. Assignments that do not require logs do not enter that process merely because logs are absent.

docs.title: Incident scope
docs.text: Local drill ID, snapshot, impact and authorized boundary. Distinguish observation from inference.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: Times of occurrence, detection, response and recovery; observations, actions and evidence.

docs.title: Causes and evidence
docs.text: Trigger conditions, contributing factors, failed assumptions and falsifiable diagnosis.

docs.title: Improvements and verification
docs.text: Role responsible for each action, checkpoints, generated fixes and regression verification. Keep the status awaiting verification until evidence is available.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: Time and roles of the human postmortem, existing evidence IDs and unresolved items. Record only activities that actually happened; do not submit a separate teaching-design form.

docs.title: Complete when permissions or data change
docs.text:
• Assets, trust boundaries, likely abuse or failure paths and mitigations (omit if not applicable):
  • Data categories, PII/key risks, redaction, access and retention (omit if not applicable):

docs.title: Review evidence
docs.text:
• Approved model review (fresh context) or TA review, review scope and evidence links:
  • Your outcome for each finding (confirmed, refuted or cannot tell) and its evidence; for cannot tell, what is missing:
  • Unresolved risks and open questions:

Respond to review feedback in the existing thread and reference revisions and re-verification results; no separate feedback form is required. Student PRs do not contain teacher pilot, hint-ladder or teaching-design records.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text: Reference the existing description and evidence ID for this assignment or milestone. Update that same description only when the purpose changes; do not repeat disclosure. Submit detailed trajectories according to the practice unit's learning objectives; per-commit Assisted-by trailers are optional.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Complete this reflection without AI assistance. Identify the related practice unit or project and learning outcomes (LOs).

docs.title: Records
docs.text: Original prediction, actual performance, failure evidence and causes of error; how to verify improvement next time. Briefly describe one prediction error, one verification step and the next improvement, without a word-count threshold. Refer to existing assignment evidence by ID rather than copying it again.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: Check the evidence yourself. If you receive feedback, record revisions and re-verification in this same note; do not submit a separate set of feedback forms.

docs.title: Goal and scope
docs.text: Users, problem, non-goals and learning outcomes (LOs).

docs.title: Interview traceability
docs.text: Interview ID / approved equivalent-material ID -> requirement ID -> acceptance criteria ID -> test ID. Do not include real names.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Given input, action, expected result, boundaries and failure paths. Each criterion must support executable verification.

docs.title: Implementation and verification
docs.text:
Generate an approach -> have a human check its assumptions -> implement inside the safe launcher -> retain acceptance and regression evidence.

Before implementation, add two scope tables and one location note to the plan:

  1. Changed files: list every file with its relevant path:line (or new for a new file). Only the files in this table may be changed; update the table and obtain another scope check before adding a file.
  2. Tests to write: list each test separately and map it to exactly one acceptance case and its expected result. Every acceptance case must have a named test; a generic “run the suite” entry is not a substitute.
  3. Specification location and update: record where this specification, its plan and decision record live, and how a code change keeps those records and acceptance tests synchronized for the next session.

docs.title: Risks and review
docs.text: Data minimization, permission boundaries, unresolved questions and review results. Refer to existing PR or review evidence; do not submit a separate teaching-design form.

docs.title: Change log
docs.text: One entry per agreed change to an acceptance criterion: the date, the changed clause, the acceptance-case and test IDs it affects, the reason and who agreed. Update those tests' expected results from the new clause first, then the code; never edit a check only to make existing code pass.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Keep the evidence needed to explain one work product. Reuse it by ID across permitted assessments.

docs.title: Artifact and decision
docs.text: Task or milestone ID, revision and the bounded change. State the user need or contract, and whether you accept, narrow, recheck or stop.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: One discriminating input with its independent expected result; the actual command/result or an explicit missing observation. Link any reused test, trace, review or participant record by ID. Keep sensitive records in the approved private location.

docs.title: My explanation and revision
docs.text: Explain why the observation supports the decision. Keep the initial prediction and one change made after feedback. Answer the changed-input question yourself. Use a few sentences; no word-count quota or full chat export.

docs.title: AI-use note
docs.text: Assistance ID; tool/model and purpose, or no AI used. Reuse this ID when the same work feeds another milestone.

docs.title: Review
docs.text: After feedback, record the one change you made and the check that supports it.
